svg.aria-label: Diagram: AWS Lambda customer-managed runtimes are a standalone resource type that fully decouples runtime management from function deployment, generally available in all commercial AWS Regions at no additional charge beyond standard Lambda and Amazon ECR pricing. A runtime version holds the contents of a customer-managed runtime and is published from a container image in Amazon ECR. Versions are immutable: after creation you cannot change the image or capabilities, and to change the runtime you create a new version. Lambda resolves the image URI to a digest returned in the ResolvedUri field, and the version always uses that digest, so moving a tag to a new image does not change the version. No function uses a new version until you point a runtime alias to it, which means the alias is the deployment, and every function that uses a customer-managed runtime must specify a runtime alias. Functions then pick up updates automatically as Lambda recycles execution environments, with no redeployment and no coordinated rollout, which also means the timing is Lambda's rather than yours. The critical dependency is that you must keep the image in Amazon ECR while the version exists: if you delete the image, functions that use the version become Inactive, a change that can take up to 24 hours, where existing execution environments continue to handle invocations but invocations that require a cold start fail, so the error rate correlates with scale-out rather than with any change you made. Deleting the repository or removing Lambda's access to the image has the same effect, an ECR lifecycle policy being the obvious automated trigger. Functions recover automatically after the image is restored, and because the version refers to the image by digest the restored image must have an identical digest rather than an equivalent rebuild. The ECR repository must be in the same Region as the runtime, may be in a different account, and must be replicated per Region. Runtime consumers do not need access to the ECR images, only permission to use the runtime, while publishers need lambda:CreateRuntimeVersion plus the ECR BatchGetImage and GetDownloadUrlForLayer actions even after granting Lambda access in the repository policy. An alias can point only to an ACTIVE version, and deleting a version schedules it with a waiting period you choose from 7 to 30 days defaulting to 30. The announcement also renames Lambda functions to Lambda Event Functions and the existing custom runtimes feature to bring your own language.
svg.title: The alias is the deployment, and the ECR image is a permanent dependency
svg.text: The runtime becomes a resource with versions and aliases. So does its blast radius.
“No function uses a new version until you point a runtime alias to it.” Publishing stages — the alias
move releases, to every consuming function at once.
The model, one level up from function versions
ECR image → runtime version (immutable, pinned to a DIGEST) → alias → functions
“If you later move the tag to a new image, the version doesn’t change.” The mutable-tag hole is closed.
Every function using a customer-managed runtime must specify an alias. It never names a version.
The dependency that did not exist before
“You must keep the image in Amazon ECR while the version exists. If you delete the image, functions that
use the version become Inactive. This change can take up to 24 hours.”
“Existing execution environments continue to handle invocations, but invocations that require a cold
start fail.” Warm traffic looks fine. Scale-out breaks. A day after the change that caused it.
WHAT TRIGGERS IT
Deleting the image · deleting the repository ·
removing Lambda’s access — “the same effect”.
An ECR lifecycle policy does all of this on a timer,
and knows nothing about runtime versions.
RECOVERY, WITH ONE CONDITION
“The functions recover automatically after you
restore the image.”
“… the restored image must have an identical
digest.” A rebuild is not the same image.
The access split is the point of the feature
“Runtime consumers don’t need access to your Amazon ECR images. They need only permission to use the
runtime.” Publishers need two ECR actions of their own — the repository policy does not cover them.
Also: repository must be same-Region (cross-account is fine) · replicate per Region · alias can point only
to an ACTIVE version · deletion waits 7 to 30 days, default 30 · updates land when Lambda recycles, not when you say.
Two renames shipped with it: functions are now Lambda Event Functions, and the old custom runtimes are “bring your own language”.
